correctness.rationale: The finite-forest frame criterion has a direct two-direction proof: no branching successor of a branching predecessor suffices, and an adjacent branching arc admits a consistent two-colour countervaluation because distinct successor subtrees are disjoint. The four labelled planted states F_{a,b} exhaust the two parent-edge orientations and two outdegree regimes with precisely one decomposition per tree. The combinatorial labelled-set construction yields four correct exact formal-series equations, and rooting gives \(z\partial T/\partial z=C+D\). The \(q^0\) coefficient uses unique sinks and Cayley. The first failed size is proven as five, with exactly 60 labelled witnesses. A standard-library checker proves no universal statement itself; it independently enumerated all labelled trees and orientations through n=7 and checked literal all-valuation modal semantics through n=6, agreeing with series counts and branch refinements.

originality.rationale: The all-valuation frame correspondence is explicitly credited to Zolin (1999), and the branching condition is not claimed as independently original. The surviving original assertion is an exact bivariate labelled enumeration over *all* orientations of *all* undirected labelled trees, with an exact four-series specification and degree-spectrum consequences. The closest published out-tree enumeration restricts to unique outward-oriented rooted trees, which neither covers nor directly implies counting all \(2^{n-1}\) orientations per unrooted tree. The prior general undirected no-adjacent-branching forest species pertains to undirected degrees, not orientation-dependent outdegrees. Literature on noncrossing orientations and asymptotic forbidden H orientations has different objects. No exact count/table was found by the reported queries. Best-knowledge priority, not certified uniqueness, is asserted.

value.rationale: The unrestricted-orientation census answers a natural, explicitly motivated quantitative validity question: how many n-world accessibility trees satisfy a non-contingency introspection axiom, with a full distribution by number of branching-out worlds? Four formal-series equations compute the all-order labelled counts and refine the spectrum, unlike fixed outward-rooted models. The exact zero-branch coefficient \(n^{n-1}\) and the sharp onset at n=5 with 60 failures clarify the extremal boundary. This is a natural complete classification/enumeration rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or a routine tiny numeric gain.
